headline: Bottled soybean oil price raised by Tk 5 per litre
summary: The maximum retail price increases to Tk 204 per litre due to rising international costs and import expenses.
details: The government has increased the maximum retail price of bottled soybean oil by Tk 5, bringing the new price to Tk 204 per litre.
Commerce Secretary Md Ataur Rahman Khan announced the decision following a meeting between the Ministry of Commerce and edible oil traders.
The price hike was triggered by higher international prices and increased import and transportation costs.
The Bangladesh Vegetable Oil Refiners’ and Vanaspati Manufacturers’ Association stated that imported edible oil costs had reached Tk 217 per litre.
Refiners claimed they had been selling bottled oil at Tk 199, resulting in a loss of approximately Tk 18 per litre over the last three months.
While the Trade and Tariff Commission recommended a Tk 10 increase, the government opted for a smaller adjustment to protect consumer interests.
Commerce Secretary Ataur Rahman Khan confirmed that prices for loose soybean oil and palm oil remain unchanged.
The government is monitoring the market to ensure stability and adequate supply, with no current shortages reported.
Refiners have accepted the Tk 5 increase with the assurance that prices may be raised further in the future.

Bottled soybean oil just got more expensive. The price has risen by Tk 5 per litre.

The government has increased the maximum retail price of bottled soybean oil by Tk 5, bringing the new price to Tk 204 per litre.

Commerce Secretary Md Ataur Rahman Khan announced the decision following a meeting between the Ministry of Commerce and edible oil traders.

The price hike was triggered by higher international prices and increased import and transportation costs.

The Bangladesh Vegetable Oil Refiners’ and Vanaspati Manufacturers’ Association stated that imported edible oil costs had reached Tk 217 per litre.

Refiners claimed they had been selling bottled oil at Tk 199, resulting in a loss of approximately Tk 18 per litre over the last three months.

While the Trade and Tariff Commission recommended a Tk 10 increase, the government opted for a smaller adjustment to protect consumer interests.

Commerce Secretary Ataur Rahman Khan confirmed that prices for loose soybean oil and palm oil remain unchanged.

The government is monitoring the market to ensure stability and adequate supply, with no current shortages reported.

Refiners have accepted the Tk 5 increase with the assurance that prices may be raised further in the future.

headline: ACC starts investigation against Asif Mahmud and 3 others over corruption
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has launched a probe into allegations of corruption involving the former advisor.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has initiated an investigation into former advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan and three others following allegations of corruption.
A spokesperson for the ACC confirmed the decision to investigate the claims against the former advisor.
In response to the probe, Asif Mahmud has called for the evidence of the allegations against him to be made public.
The investigation is part of the commission's efforts to address corruption allegations involving high-profile individuals.
